READING

**Framing the choice**

Both courses are one-time capital commitments on top of an ongoing business. The right comparison is therefore not just the headline outlay but what each course actually buys in operational terms, for how long, and at what running cost.

---

**The financial arithmetic**

Extra capital required by VELLACOTT over TARNSIDE: £2,680,000 − £1,730,000 = **£950,000**.

Annual fuel saving from VELLACOTT: **£190,000**.

Simple payback on that extra £950,000: £950,000 ÷ £190,000 = **5.0 years** — so by roughly 2032, VELLACOTT has repaid its own premium purely from lower fuel bills, with no other factors counted. Every year after that, VELLACOTT is £190,000 ahead per annum.

That is the core financial signal and it is unambiguous beyond the five-year mark.

---

**What the money actually buys**

*TARNSIDE* spends £1,730,000 and keeps a 1995-built hull. After re-engining in 2027 the Brindlemere will be 32 years old. The hull survey was clean, but hull surveys are point-in-time; a 1995 structure will generate rising maintenance, inspection, and eventually steelwork costs as she moves through her late thirties. The "original engines gave out" problem simply re-presents in a different form in the mid-2030s. TARNSIDE defers the vessel-replacement question; it does not resolve it.

*VELLACOTT* spends £2,680,000 net and acquires a 2017-built vessel. In 2026 she is nine years old. If Cormorant Sound runs her to a typical 30-year ferry lifespan, the Suilvenaig has roughly 20 years of primary life ahead. That is the meaningful distinction: this is not just a cheaper-fuel swap, it is a generational vessel renewal.

---

**Staffing**

Losing two of nine masters to retirement is a real cost. Seven masters on a single-vessel rota is tighter, but not unworkable — particularly in winter (five crossings/day). The six-week endorsement course for the remaining seven is an immediate logistical pressure because the handover window is 2026-11-20, which is 87 days from today. Starting the first one or two masters on the course in early September would yield endorsements in mid-October, giving a margin before handover. That is tight but achievable with immediate action. Recruiting one replacement master over the following year would restore comfortable rota depth, and a new hire could be selected for the endorsement from the outset.

The two retirements and the course fees (not quoted in the figures provided) are genuine omitted costs that should be confirmed, but they are unlikely to be large enough to close a £950,000 payback gap.

---

**Insurance**

This is the most material unresolved variable. The Suilvenaig's insured hull value will be roughly five times the Brindlemere's, so even at a comparable rate the absolute premium will be higher. The broker must be asked for an indicative quote before any heads of terms are signed; if the insurance increase runs to, say, £50,000/year, payback shifts from 5.0 years to 6.3 years — still well within the vessel's working life. Only a very large premium movement would materially alter the decision, and a 2017-built vessel on a licensed route should not attract punitive terms. The absence of a quote is an information gap, not a negative signal.

---

**Timing of the Brindlemere sale**

Kittiwake's £610,000 valuation holds until 2027-02-11. If VELLACOTT is chosen, the Brindlemere must be marketed promptly after Suilvenaig handover. If the sale slips past February 2027, a fresh valuation would be needed. This is manageable but requires active attention.

---

**Yard period**

The 12-week yard period for TARNSIDE runs from 2027-01-05, which falls in the off-peak winter schedule (five crossings/day). A charter at £310,000 covers it. The disruption is real but seasonal, and VELLACOTT avoids it entirely. This is not decisive either way, but it adds to TARNSIDE's complexity without adding any long-term value.

---

**Summary balance**

| Factor | TARNSIDE | VELLACOTT |
|---|---|---|
| Net capital outlay | £1,730,000 | £2,680,000 |
| Annual fuel cost | £190,000/yr worse | Baseline |
| Payback crossover | — | ~5 years |
| Vessel age in 2030 | 35 years | 13 years |
| Masters | 9, no course needed | 7, course needed immediately |
| Insurance | Known | Must be confirmed |
| Yard period / charter | 12 weeks, £310k | None |
| Next replacement horizon | Mid-2030s likely | Mid-2040s or later |

The case for TARNSIDE rests on lower upfront cost, known insurance, and no staffing disruption. These are real advantages. The case against it is that you spend £1.73 million to preserve a 1995 hull you will need to replace again in a decade or so anyway, at higher fuel cost throughout.

The case for VELLACOTT rests on a five-year payback on the premium, £190,000/year savings thereafter, and a vessel with twenty-plus years of primary working life. The risks — insurance, endorsements, reduced master pool — are all addressable in the near term and none of them is structural.

Conditional recommendation: proceed with VELLACOTT, with two immediate actions required before commitment: (1) obtain the insurance indicative quote, and (2) confirm at least one master can begin the endorsement course in September 2026. If the insurance quote is not materially adverse, VELLACOTT is clearly the stronger course.

---

READING
The £950,000 premium of VELLACOTT over TARNSIDE is repaid by fuel savings in five years; the unresolved insurance and master-endorsement issues are both addressable in the near term; and the fundamental problem with TARNSIDE is that re-engining a 1995 hull does not resolve the vessel-replacement question — it merely postpones it by a decade at higher running cost, after which a much larger capital decision returns. VELLACOTT buys a generational renewal; TARNSIDE buys time.

CALL
VELLACOTT

GROUNDS
The £950,000 additional capital VELLACOTT demands over TARNSIDE is recovered entirely by fuel savings within five years, after which every subsequent year runs £190,000 cheaper aboard a nine-year-old hull with decades of working life remaining, whereas re-engining the Brindlemere preserves a thirty-one-year-old vessel whose replacement question simply returns in the mid-2030s.
